[[Deep North]] |Snow-capped hills and forests with frozen rivers, inhabited by [[Moose]], [[Elaking]], and [[Gammeltroll|Gammeltrolls]]. |Northern edge of the world |} == Alternative biomes == Each biome patch has a chance to have modifiers applied to it on world generation, but only a certain distance from the world center. These modifiers can have the following effects: * Affect foliage, like more [[Raspberries]] or only [[Birch]]es in the Meadows, or only stubs in the Black Forest * Generate additional structures, like [[Large Bone]]s in the Swamps, Plains or Mistlands, or more [[Tar Pit]]s in the Plains * Increase the chance for [[creature level|starred]] creatures * Enable the spawning of certain creatures not normally encountered in the biome, such as [[Bat]]s in the Swamp, or increase existing chances for a creature to spawn, like more [[Abomination]]s * Disable the spawning of creatures native to the biome Several modifiers can affect a single area at once. The following biomes can be affected: * [[Meadows#Alternative biomes|Meadows]] has 8 modifiers. * [[Black Forest#Alternative biomes|Black Forests]] have 8 modifiers. * [[Swamp#Alternative biomes|Swamps]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Mountains]] have 3 modifiers. * [[Plains#Alternative biomes|Plains]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mistlands#Alternative biomes|Mistlands]] have 6 modifiers. Oceans, the Ashlands and the Deep North do not have any alternative variants. ==Trivia== *The term "biome" comes from the [[wikipedia:biome|ecological concept of the same name]]. *At ''Valheim's'' early access launch in February 2021, five of the planned nine biomes were made available to explore. The other four were accessible, but lacked any meaningful content. ** As of the full release in September 2026, all biomes excluding the Ocean are fully implemented. An Ocean overhaul was ultimately abandoned, with the argument that it only serves the role of a highway between other biomes, which do have meaningful content. * Alternative biomes were introduced in the [[1.0]] release. {{Biomes}} [[de:Biom]] [[ru:Биомы]] [[pt-br:Biomas]] [[uk:Біоми]] [[cs:Biomy]] [[zh-tw:生物群落]] [[Category:Biomes| ]]

[[File:Greyling 0S.png|thumb|A [[greyling]], an aggressive creature found in the [[Meadows]].]] '''Creatures''' are non-player characters which are found throughout ''[[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]''. They can be split to four categories: * [[Creatures#Bosses|Bosses]] are powerful aggressive creatures that must be summoned. Killing them unlocks [[Forsaken power|Forsaken powers]], increases [[Global Keys|world difficulty]] and provides loot to progress in the game. * [[Creatures#Minibosses|Minibosses]] are unique, named, aggressive creatures that you can find in specific dungeons. Killing any given miniboss will reward with one of [[Hildir's Chests]]. * [[Creatures#Aggressive creatures|Aggressive creatures]] will attack players when alerted. They also drop loot when killed. * [[Creatures#Passive creatures|Passive creatures]] provide resources when killed (or harvested). They will never attack players. * [[Creatures#NPCs|NPCs]] are friendly creatures/characters that cannot be killed and may provide some service or help to the player. == Bosses == Bosses, also known as the '''Forsaken''', can be summoned by offering specific items (hinted by the [[Runestone#Altar Runestones|Runestones]]) at their specific spawn site. They have increased HP and special attacks compared to regular creatures. A boss site is automatically marked on the player's map by reading the runestone in the specific biomes. There are multiple spawn locations for every boss. One-star creatures have double the health and deal 150% damage, while two-stars have triple the health and deal double damage. '''Behavior''' *Creatures will give up chasing after unable to attack for 60 seconds or unable to detect the target for 30 seconds. *Some creatures have a max chase range. After chasing that far they will give up if unable to detect the target for 1 seconds. *After unable to attack for 15 seconds, creatures will focus structures for 15 seconds if they can't reach the target. *Creatures only attack walls and doors if they aren't able to reach the target player. *Some creatures are afraid of fire and will flee from it. *Some creatures try to avoid fire and will be passive near it. *Some creatures circulate around the target while waiting to attack. *Swimming creatures try to flee towards water if forced on ground. *Creatures passively regenerate 1.67% of their max health every minute (100% over 60 minutes). *Creatures gain +30% more effective health per each additional player within 100 meters. E.g. 3 players = +60% effective health. **This is updated whenever the creature takes damage. *Creatures gain +4% more damage per each additional player within 100 meters. '''Mushrooms''' can be found on the ground in the [[Meadows]], [[Black Forest]] and [[Swamp]]. Picked mushrooms will respawn after 240 minutes, or {{duration|14400}}, at the same place that they were picked. Unlike the case with raspberries and blueberries, which do not return if the plant itself is removed, mushrooms will return if the ground is cleared or even excavated.

Mushrooms are almost negligible as a food, but they are a vital component of some of the best recipes in the later game, as well as being food for tame Boars. Since they cannot be cultivated, and do not grow in large numbers at any one place, it is prudent to save some of them from early in the game for later use.

== Collection strategies ==
Collecting large quantities of mushrooms can be tedious since they cannot be farmed with a cultivator. However, there are strategies to make mushroom collection more manageable. One of the simplest and most effective methods is to mark mushroom locations on your map. This can be done from the start of the game, helping you plan efficient foraging routes.

Additionally, once you have enough resources to create multiple portals, you can set up "portal chains" for rapid mushroom collection. Start by placing a portal at your base with a short name ending in "1". Travel to an area with a large mushroom patch, link up the first portal, and set up a new portal with the same name ending in "2", and continue to another mushroom-rich area. Repeat this process as many times as needed. Finally, place a return portal at the last location and link it back to your base. This setup allows for quick and easy mushroom collection every 240 minutes.

To keep track of the harvest time, use a pickable ground item near your mushroom portal to act as a timer. Since all ground items respawn every 240 minutes (4 hours), picking up an item at your base after a mushroom harvest will signal when it is time to harvest again once the item reappears.

}} '''Birch''' is a type of tree that can be found in the [[Meadows]] and [[Plains]] biomes. It is characterized by its white bark with black spots. A [[Bronze Axe]] or better is required to damage it. Birch trees produce [[Wood]] and [[Finewood]] when destroyed. The yield of each type of wood is random, however, a birch tree will always drop 20 pieces of wood total (plus 2 Wood from its stump). It is possible to damage Birch trees by intentionally hitting them with falling [[Beech]] trees. If enough damage is done by falling trees, the Birch tree will be brought down. The trunk can then be rolled downslope (ideally) and repeatedly smashed into obstacles until it shatters into usable lumber. Birch trees can also be destroyed by a [[Troll]]. These methods allow players to acquire [[Finewood]] before being able to craft a [[Bronze Axe]]. Birch trees come in 4 variations: two different shapes, each of which has two biome-dependent variations (which differ in color but not in shape). The two shapes can be distinguished by the number and position of their branches: Variation 1 has fewer large branches, the lowest of which is about 8 meters from the ground, while Variation 2 has a very thick branch which splits from the trunk at only about 4 meters from the ground, and more large branches up higher. Each of these shapes can come in two colors: with green leaves (in non-Plains [[Biomes]]) or with yellow leaves (in Plains only). Each Birch tree's color is dependent entirely on which biome it spawns in, but its shape is determined entirely randomly. Player-grown Birch trees always have green foliage. == Health == A birch tree has 80 health. When felled, it drops one large log with 60 health, which breaks into two small logs with 60 health each. The stump has 80 health. All parts can only be damaged with chop damage and require a tool of tier 2 or higher, such as the [[Bronze Axe]]; the stump can also be broken with a pickaxe of the same tier, such as the [[Iron Pickaxe]]. == Drops == Below, variants are abbreviated according to shape (1 or 2, as defined above) and by color ("G" for green or "Y" for yellow). This attack can be used every 5 seconds when within 2 meters of a player. == Taming == ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming]].'' To tame a wild Boar, players should approach while sneaking to avoid alarming it. If a Boar feels threatened, it will become aggressive, chasing the player until they are out of sight, at which point it will revert to a 'hungry' state. Wild Boars have a predictable combat pattern, charging and then retreating, which can be used to the player's advantage when herding them into a pen ''(recommended to tame)''. Constructing a secure pen is essential to prevent the Boar from escaping and to avoid disruption of the taming process by outside sources. To successfully tame a Boar, players need to feed it {{item link|Raspberries}}, {{item link|Blueberries}}, {{item link|Carrot}}s, {{item link|Onion}}s, {{item link|Turnip}}s, or red {{item link|Mushroom}}s. They will ignore all other foods dropped on the ground. Just drop the food on the ground within one meter, and the Boar will eat, as long as it is not frightened ''(indicated by a red exclamation mark)''. Players can place the food on the ground in a stack, as the Boar will only eat one food from the stack at a time. The taming speed is 30 minutes of real-life gameplay with three pieces of food, '''uninterrupted'''; as long as the Boar does not get frightened and the correct amount of food is on the ground, it should only take 30 minutes. A player must remain in the area for taming to progress. If the Boar becomes frightened at any time during taming, the process will take longer and may require more food. == Tamed == When tamed, Boars seek freedom. If a tamed Boar sees an opening in their fenced area, they will run towards it, which can be used to corral them from place to place. Tamed Boars can be renamed by pressing LShift + E. Interacting with them using E will display the message "(Creature name) loves you" on-screen along with a cloud of pink hearts. They are no longer afraid of fire and require feeding for passive health regeneration. Additionally, tamed Boars lose their anchor to their spawn point, allowing them to move more freely. '''Note:''' ''Boars from abandoned farms and Runestones will retain their anchor point and will always try to return home, making them more challenging to handle. It is recommended to either breed these boars on the spot and move the offspring instead, or to name the original tamed animal and then, once bred, kill it. One issue with using the original animal is that it tends to sit in a corner of a pen, staring at its spawn point, which can interfere with breeding as it does not roam the pen.'' == Breeding == Tamed Boars can breed, provided the Boar is happy and well-fed with berries, carrots, onions, turnips or red mushrooms, along with there being another Boar at least within three meters, and no more than five Boars within at least 10 meters. Once the conditions are met, the Boar will accumulate love points (3) with one another until the pregnancy starts. Successful love point is indicated by pink hearts. After gaining enough love points, the Boar becomes pregnant, which is not visualized. After one minute, the Boar gives birth to a baby Boar ''(piglet)'', visualized by a red cloud. Any Boar can become pregnant, which means that if two Boars breed and one becomes pregnant, they still have the ability to breed and get the other pregnant. Once born, the '''piglet''' will take 50 minutes to mature into an adult. Offspring inherit [[Creature Level|stars]] from the parent that gives birth to it. Offspring are tamed at birth and require a [[Butcher Knife]] or friendly fire to kill. They village made of various Fuling themed structures. ==Resources== Fuling Village are protected by numerous [[Fuling]]s, [[Fuling Shaman]]s and [[Fuling Berserker]]s. Notable resources are: * Small patches of 12 planted [[Barley]] ready to harvest for two barley each. * Small patches of 11 planted [[Flax]] ready to harvest for two flax each. * Next to each [[Bonfire]] there is a 50% chance for a [[Fuling Totem]] on an altar. * [[Loot chest#Plains Chest|Plains Chest]] can be found in various places. * [[Tanning Rack]] can be destroyed for 6 [[Leather Scraps]], 5 [[Flint]] and a [[Deer Hide]]. * Huts can be destroyed for various quantities of Deer hide, [[Bone Fragments]] and [[Wood]]. == Strategy == When raiding a Fuling village, it is highly recommended to use a bow to dispatch the Fulings from afar. Thinning their numbers with ranged attacks before attempting melee combat is exceedingly effective. A fully upgraded [[Draugr Fang]] armed with [[Poison Arrow]]s or [[Needle Arrow]]s is capable of killing a normal, unaware Fuling in a single shot. Aggroing too many Fulings at once may result in the player being overwhelmed. Picking off Fulings with arrows will cut down on the number of enemies to fight, and it will often aggro small groups, which will be far easier to fight than the whole village. Target the sentries in towers and Fuling shamans first: shooting sentries will draw away other Fulings near the tower, and shamans will shield themselves and other Fulings nearby with magic if they are alerted. Running away is always a valid strategy if the player has enough energy to do so. == Notes == * Fuling villages will often be populated by a substantial number of [[Fuling]]s, [[Fuling Shaman]]s, and [[Fuling Berserker]]s. It is not advised that ill-equipped players enter the village; [[Iron]] armor and weapons or better are recommended. * Be aware that chopping down trees in close proximity to a Fuling village may cause Fulings to investigate. If you retreat before they are alerted to your presence, they will return to their village. ==Gallery== Frick.png | A Fuling village swarming a Silver Age Viking. '''Forsaken powers''' are unlocked by defeating each boss and hanging their trophy on the [[Sacrificial Stones]]. By default, the player's set forsaken power is activated by [[Controls|pressing F]]. Only one forsaken power can be set at a time, which is changed out at the Sacrificial Stones.

All forsaken powers have a duration of 5 minutes. They also share the same 20-minute cooldown, which does not reset or reduce even when the player logs off, changes their active forsaken power, or sleeps.  

Activating a power locks the player into an animation for a couple of seconds. The player is unable to move or perform any action (with the exception of equipping or unequipping tools/weapons). 

When activating a forsaken power, all players within 10 meters will also receive the benefit of the forsaken power activated. Thus, a party of four players can keep a forsaken power activated virtually indefinitely by consecutively using each player's forsaken power. 

==[[Eikthyr]] Power==
{{Quote|The grace of the mighty stag flows through you. Your ability to move around is improved, be it on land or in water.}}
60% reduced [[stamina]] usage for running, jumping, and swimming.

==[[The Elder]] Power==
{{Quote|The power of the forest invigorates you. You shall gather its bounties faster, just as you shall regain your own vitality should you lose it.}}
+60% [[Chop]] and [[Pickaxe]] damage increase, +30% health regeneration increase.

==[[Bonemass]] Power==
{{Quote|The mass takes the brunt of your blows. The effort required to raise your shield lessens, and you can withstand harder hits.}}
[[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] (-25%) VS pierce, slash, and blunt damage, -100% [[block]] stamina cost, +5 stamina returned per block.

==[[Moder]] Power==
{{Quote|The dragon's wings urge you on. You shall always have tailwind while sailing, and you shall swiftly carry heavy burdens, even over the coldest mountains.}}
Always tailwind when sailing, +300.0 increased [[carry weight]], +10% increased movement speed, [[Resistance|Resistant]] (-50%) vs frost.

===Notes===
*This power changes the [[wind]] direction while sailing, but not wind intensity. A calm wind will not aid in travel as much as a fast wind.
*The wind direction is only changed while steering the ship. While not in control of a ship, the wind will remain at its regular angle.
*The wind change is local to each player carrying the buff and does not affect each other's wind direction.
*This power is best saved for when there is headwind since crosswind (perpendicular to travel direction) and tailwind are about equally good for sailing.
*This power will not affect the wind if you are too close to the [[World Edge|World's Edge]].

==[[Yagluth]] Power==
{{Quote|The fallen king lends you his might. A king must have the power to vanquish his foes, just as he must be able to support his people.}}
Resistant (-50%) vs lightning, +25 [[Farming (skill)]], and +10% increased damage.

{{Quote|Her Majesty blesses you. In her shadow both stealth and magic may flourish, and no poison shall harm you.}}
+100% [[Eitr]] regeneration increase, -100% [[sneak]] stamina usage, and resistant (-50%) vs poison.

'''Obliterators''' are buildable structures that convert any item to [[Coal]]. 

== Usage ==
Put gifts to Thor into the Obliterator and pull the lever on the right side, giving the player coal in return.

When activated, lightning strikes the lightning rod above the Obliterator dealing 400 [[Damage types|Lightning]] damage and additional 10 [[Damage types|Lightning]] damage within 2.42 meters.
== Conversion rates ==
To get 1 coal, insert:
*1 [[Trophies|Trophy]], including boss trophies, except trophies from [[Ashlands]] creatures, [[Hildir]] minibosses, [[Bear]], [[Vile]] and [[Ghost]].
*5 [[Wood]], [[Corewood]], [[Finewood]], [[Ancient Bark]], or [[Yggdrasil Wood]].
*20 [[Arrows]], except ([[Charred Arrow]])
*20 [[Bolts]], except ([[Iron Bolt]] and [[Charred Bolt]])
*10 of other items (including coal)

== Notes ==
* The Obliterator can be placed anywhere on a flat surface and does not degrade due to rain.
* The Obliterator generates its own lightning bolt and does not require a thunderstorm to operate.
* Wood and meats can be converted to coal at a 1:1 conversion rate using a [[Charcoal Kiln]] or cooking station, making it resource-inefficient to place these in the Obliterator. 
* Currently, many trophies after Mistlands do not share the 1:1 conversion rate as other trophies, including Hildir's minibosses.

Hen are tameable birds that can reproduce and will lay eggs under certain conditions, including being fed with any of: {{Item link|Dandelion}}, {{Item link|Beech Seeds}}, {{Item link|Birch Seeds}}, {{Item link|Carrot Seeds}}, {{Item link|Turnip Seeds}}, {{Item link|Onion Seeds}}, or {{Item link|Barley}} (''not'' {{Item link|Barley Flour}}).

== Obtain ==
Hens are grown up chickens. A chicken will grow up after a certain amount of time (approximately two days) after an egg has hatched. [[Egg]]s can be bought for 1500 [[Coins]] from [[Haldor]], or found as loot in [[Sealed Tower|Sealed Towers]].

'''Ballistae''' are [[:Category:Misc structures|misc structures]] that act as an automated defense. 

A Ballista can hold 40 missiles of the same type, which will be depleted one at a time as it fires. By default, a Ballista will shoot at any [[Creatures|creature]] in an arc (±45 degrees) within a 28 meters range in front of it, including [[Player Character|player characters]] and [[Taming|tamed]] animals. Care should be taken when loading the Ballista, as it will begin shooting after the first missile is loaded if the player is standing within the firing arc.

Damage is solely based upon the [[Missiles|missile]] loaded ([[Wooden Missile]], [[Black Metal Missile]], or [[Flametal Missile]]).

==Targeting==
Targeting can be overridden by using [[trophies]]. The Ballista will usually only target and shoot enemies corresponding to the trophy used, with the exception of Draugr and Charred enemies. 
* Using trophies from [[Draugr]] or [[Draugr Elite]] will set the Ballista to target 'Draugr', including melee and ranged variants, as well as the Draugr Elite. 
* Using trophies from the [[Charred Warrior]], [[Charred Marksman]], or the [[Charred Warlock]] will set the Ballista to target 'Charred', including all of these enemies as well as the [[Charred Twitcher]]. 
* Only one trophy can be active at once, and it is not consumed, allowing for a single trophy to be used on any number of Ballistae. 
* Default targeting can be applied by using the same trophy again, or by dismantling and rebuilding the Ballista.

== Notes ==
* Considering their hostility to friendlies, such as other players and tames, in default targeting mode, caution and placement location is highly advised. Building structures which can be opened and closed, such as [[Wood Structures|wooden doors or wooden gates]], in front of the Ballista to block their field of vision ensures safe passing when needed.
* Ballistae have a slow and inaccurate aim, but quick shooting speed. Building [[Trap|traps]] to immobilize fast-moving enemies in the Ballista's range increase their effectiveness greatly. For bigger and/or slower enemies, the Ballista might need higher elevation to be effective, especially against flying creatures.
* Due to its universal target range, Ballistae can be used to train blocking skills. However, Ballistae ''cannot be parried'', so using [[Shields|tower shields]] in combination with wooden missiles due to lower damage is recommended. They can also serve as protection against other players in multiplayer servers, while still being mindful of the Ballista targeting its owner.
